title: Assessing readiness for transfer to adult care in adolescents with long-term conditions: a narrative review of measurement, prediction and experience
abstract: Readiness questionnaires are widely used to time transfer from paediatric to adult care. This narrative review, based on a documented search, examines what readiness tools measure, whether scores predict outcomes after transfer, how young people and families experience assessment, and how assessment can be fair for disadvantaged groups. Findings and implications will be written after the synthesis.
introduction: Transition clinics often use readiness scores to decide when adolescents transfer, but the evidence that scores predict how young people do after transfer is limited.
methods: Three databases and two grey literature sources were searched from 2010 with a dated strategy; sources were selected purposively for four questions and synthesised thematically, with the strength of evidence stated for each conclusion.
results: No sources have been synthesised yet. The review will present the constructs measured, prediction findings by condition, experience themes and approaches for disadvantaged groups.
discussion: The discussion will set out what readiness assessment can and cannot do and propose how a clinic can use it for planning rather than as a threshold.
limitations: Narrative selection, English only, and prediction evidence concentrated in type 1 diabetes.
conclusion: To be written after the synthesis.
summary: Narrative review draft with findings left empty.
